summary_en: By decree of 25 January 2021, at the mandate of Pope Francis, three optional memorials are inscribed in the General Roman Calendar: St Gregory of Narek, abbot and Doctor of the Church, on 27 February; St John De Avila, priest and Doctor of the Church, on 10 May; St Hildegard of Bingen, virgin and Doctor of the Church, on 17 September. The new memorials are to be inserted in every Calendar and liturgical book for Mass and the Liturgy of the Hours; the Latin decree (p. 122) is followed by English, French, German, Spanish, Italian and Portuguese versions (pp. 123-127) and by the annexed 'Additiones in libris liturgicis' (pp. 128-135: Calendar, Missal collects, Ordo lectionum nn. 536bis, 561bis, 641bis, Liturgy of the Hours, and new Martyrology elogia to be added in first place on 27 February and 10 May and in second place on 17 September). The Nota circa i testi liturgici (Prot. 35/21-40/21, pp. 146-151) confirms that in the Martyrologium Romanum the elogia of these saints, now carrying the title of Doctor, take those places. The decree's own Latin text (p. 122) has no printed page number.
excerpt: Summus Pontifex FRANCISCUS in Calendarium Romanum generale inseri decrevit subsequentes celebrationes, gradu memoriæ ad libitum: sancti Gregorii Narecensis, abbatis et Ecclesiæ doctoris, die 27 mensis Februarii, sancti Ioannis De Avila, presbyteri et Ecclesiæ doctoris, die 10 mensis Maii, sanctæ Hildegardis Bingensis, virginis et Ecclesiæ doctoris, die 17 mensis Septembris.

summary_en: By decree of 26 January 2021, at the mandate of Pope Francis, the memorial of 29 July in the General Roman Calendar, hitherto of St Martha alone, becomes the memorial of Saints Martha, Mary and Lazarus; the memorial is to appear under this title in all Calendars and liturgical books for Mass and the Liturgy of the Hours. Latin decree (p. 136) followed by English, French, German, Spanish, Italian and Portuguese versions (pp. 136-141) and by the annexed 'Variationes et additiones' (pp. 142-145: Calendar entry '29 Ss. Marthæ, Mariæ et Lazari, Memoria', Missal formulary with new collect, Ordo lectionum n. 607, Liturgy of the Hours, and a new Martyrology elogium replacing the first elogium of 29 July, with elogium n. 2 omitted; the Nota, pp. 146-151, lists which texts are new). The API key StsMarthaMaryLazarus is used in the lectionary data while the 1970 Missal key is StMartha.
excerpt: Summus Pontifex FRANCISCUS, annuens huius Dicasterii propositis, disposuit ut memoria sanctorum Marthæ, Mariæ et Lazari in Calendario Romano generali die 29 iulii inscriberetur. Hac denominatione memoria igitur ista cunctis Calendariis et Libris liturgicis pro Missæ et Liturgiæ Horarum celebratione indicanda erit

summary_en: General executive decree 'Postquam Summus Pontifex' implementing can. 838 CIC after the motu proprio Magnum Principium (approved by Pope Francis, dated 22 October 2021). Its section 'De Dioecesium et Familiarum Religiosarum propriis' (nn. 50-55) restates that dioceses, institutes of consecrated life, societies of apostolic life and others with the right have their own particular Calendar, Proper of Masses and of the Liturgy of the Hours and Martyrology; that proper celebrations are inserted harmoniously into the General Roman Calendar, the diocesan calendar taking account of national and regional calendars; that every particular Calendar drawn up by the competent authority must be approved by the Apostolic See, the competent authority (bishop, superior or superior general) requesting the 'recognitio' of the Calendar and Proper from the Congregation with a report on the reasons for each variation or inscription of celebrations. Part II 'Variationes' (pp. 215-222) amends the praenotanda of the liturgical books accordingly, including Martyrologium Romanum praenotanda nn. 38 and 41 on the Proprium Martyrologii. Latin text pp. 152-161, followed by Italian, English, French, German and Spanish versions (pp. 162-214). Flagged for review: a procedural norm on particular calendars rather than an act naming a calendar or celebration.
excerpt: 51. Celebrationes propriae in Calendarium Romanum generale congruenter inseruntur. Calendarium liturgicum dioecesanum prae oculis Calendarium nationale et regionale habere oportet. Omnia Calendaria particularia, a competenti auctoritate confecta, ab Apostolica Sede approbari debent.
